subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

judge.implied_focus: The nature and resolution of the underlying technical failure described in each incident ticket (what broke, why, and what it takes to fix it).

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Identifies the affected component/system (printer, monitor, network), grounding what kind of thing failed -- a core facet of the failure focus.

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: Directly characterizes the mode of failure (service failure, unresponsive, physical damage), central to the implied focus.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: Captures what fix is required (repair, replacement, config), a natural downstream facet of failure characterization.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: Indicates whether the failure resolved without intervention, a coherent outcome facet tied to failure handling.

per_column.name: is_repeat_incident_type
per_column.rationale: Flags recurrence of the failure type, an analytically useful attribute of the failure pattern (though the 452/48 skew is suspect).

per_column.name: urgency_signal
per_column.rationale: Derived urgency of the failure from the description, a reasonable severity facet, mildly redundant with existing priority.

judge.rationale: The six columns cohere tightly around a single inferable focus: characterizing the technical failure behind each incident and its resolution. They form a sound multi-facet structure -- affected component (incident_category), failure mode (failure_type), required fix (resolution_action_type), and outcome/severity attributes (self_resolved, is_repeat_incident_type, urgency_signal) -- all extractable from short_description rather than restating existing structured fields. This is not a grab-bag nor a single restatement, and the focus is genuinely actionable (an analyst could prioritize fixes, target recurring failure classes, or reduce repair volume). Minor deductions: urgency_signal partially overlaps existing priority, and the extreme skews on is_repeat_incident_type (90% true) and self_resolved suggest weaker/coarser inference on those facets, slightly reducing structure quality.
